children: Xiaomi's third-quarter profit fell sharply on weaker revenue and margins as the Chinese technology company faced a host of challenges--from weaker smartphone demand to a slowing auto market in China.
The Beijing-based company on Tuesday said net profit slumped 68% from a year earlier to 3.88 billion yuan. Revenue declined 5.2% to 107.24 billion yuan.
Analysts had expected net profit of 4.97 billion yuan on revenue of 106.92 billion yuan, according to a Visible Alpha consensus.

Revenue from smartphones, Xiaomi's largest business, fell 0.8% to 46.0 billion yuan. Shipments dropped 20% to 30.7 million units in the third quarter, partly due to lower shipments of its low-end smartphones globally, the company said. Its average selling price for smartphones reached a record high of 1,486 yuan, a 40% increase from the previous year.
Bernstein analysts said ahead of the results that Xiaomi's shift toward more premium products helped cushion the impact to earnings from weak smartphone shipments.

The Internet-of-Things and lifestyle products segment--which includes washing machines, vacuums and other appliances--was another drag. Segment sales declined 1.45% to 27.15 billion yuan due to lower revenue from certain lifestyle products, though that was partially offset by higher revenue from laptops and smart large home appliances as well as tablets in overseas markets, the company said.
Higher component costs and weaker sales led to an overall gross margin of 20.2% for the three months ended September, down from 22.9% a year earlier, the company said.
Xiaomi's electric-vehicle business also faced pressures from slowing demand in the domestic market, with revenue declining 20% to 22.7 billion yuan.
